stories.title: How to Track Your Luggage (2026): AirTag, Pebblebee, CaseSafe
stories.summary: The Wired Reviews article offers practical advice for stress‑free travel, emphasizing the importance of tracking luggage when checked‑in items become unavoidable. The author shares a personal anecdote about a surprise propeller flight that forced carry‑ons to be gate‑checked, and how Bluetooth trackers helped him confirm his suitcases stayed with him through layovers. The piece encourages readers to avoid checked bags whenever possible but provides tips for those that must be checked, including using trackable cases. It highlights the July “Trackable Carry‑On” from CaseSafe as the only carry‑on sized sufficiently small (21.5 × 15 × 8.5 in) to fit in the overhead bin of a DHC‑8‑400, noting its slim dimensions and built‑in tracking feature. The article also directs readers to related reviews on the best carry‑on suitcases, travel totes, and laptop backpacks.

stories.title: Five Eyes spook shops warn rapid rollouts of agentic AI are too risky
stories.summary: A joint Five Eyes guidance document—issued last Friday by Australia, the United States, Canada, New Zealand and the United Kingdom—warns that agentic AI systems, which autonomously act across critical infrastructure and defense, are likely to misbehave and expand an organisation’s attack surface. The guide cites illustrative scenarios (e.g., an AI patch‑manager deleting firewall logs or a procurement bot enabling fraud after a low‑risk tool is compromised) to show how even well‑designed agents can be abused. It lists 23 specific risks, over 100 mitigation practices, and stresses that developers, vendors and security teams must test, fail‑safe‑design, and human‑escalate uncertain actions. The report urges a highly cautious, incremental rollout that prioritises resilience, reversibility and risk containment over efficiency, demanding strong governance, accountability, monitoring and oversight until mature security standards for agentic AI emerge.

stories.title: Can Listening to ‘Subliminals’ Make You Beautiful? Plenty of Women Believe It
stories.summary: The article explores the rise of “subliminal” videos—short audio‑visual clips that embed hypnotic affirmations aimed at reshaping viewers’ self‑image and external appearance—on platforms like TikTok and Reddit. With millions of views, these clips promise everything from flawless skin to ideal body proportions, and even broader life gains such as academic success or romantic attraction. While originally rooted in a niche 2012 subreddit, the trend has expanded to cover a wide array of “looksmaxxing,” “facemaxxing,” and “beautymaxxing” content, echoing the anxieties driving male looks‑maximizers into radical online cultures. The article highlights how young women, pressured by unrealistic beauty standards, increasingly turn to these quasi‑spiritual tools instead of traditional fitness or medical approaches, citing anecdotal reports of significant personal change and the emergence of self‑made subliminal creators.

stories.title: Science Has Found Even More Ways Coffee Is Good for You
stories.summary: A recent study published in *Nature Communications* examined how regular coffee drinking affects the gut‑brain axis in healthy adults, distinguishing caffeine’s role from other coffee compounds. Thirty‑one habitual coffee drinkers (3–5 cups daily) and thirty‑one non‑drinkers were compared, and participants also cycled through two‑week coffee abstinence followed by re‑introduction of either caffeinated or decaffeinated coffee. The results showed that coffee alters gut microbiota composition—boosting species such as *Eggerthella* and *Cryptobacterium curtum*—and reduces inflammatory markers while increasing anti‑inflammatory molecules, effects that persist even with decaffeinated coffee. Behaviorally, regular drinkers exhibited higher impulsiveness and emotional reactivity, which eased during the abstinence period, and both coffee types lowered perceived stress and depressive symptoms; caffeine‑rich coffee further improved anxiety and attention, whereas decaf enhanced memory, sleep quality, and activity. Cortisol levels remained unchanged, suggesting coffee mainly influences subjective stress perception. Overall, the study highlights coffee’s complex, caffeine‑independent modulation of the microbiome, metabolism, and neuro‑behavioral states, supporting its potential as a dietary intervention for gut and mental health.

stories.title: 15 Best MagSafe Wireless Chargers (2026): Power Banks, Stands, Pads, and Travel Chargers
stories.summary: The article reviews a range of MagSafe‑compatible Qi2 wireless chargers that didn’t earn top honors. The Mous Dual Charging Station offers dual pads (15 W MagSafe, 5 W Qi) plus a USB‑C port but is slow. Anker’s MagGo delivers a sturdy 15 W pad with a built‑in cable, while Belkin’s BoostCharge Pro converts into a stand and charges up to 15 W. Casetify’s PowerThru 2‑in‑1 charges iPhones at 7.5 W and earbuds at 15 W, and its cheaper single‑pad version offers 7.5 W MagSafe or 15 W Qi with a decorative design. Mophie’s 3‑in‑1 travel charger packs iPhone, Watch, and AirPods charging (15 W) in a fold‑out case. All options blend design variety with modest charging speeds, providing alternatives for those seeking MagSafe convenience at different price points.

stories.title: Dating Is a Rich Person’s Game Now
stories.summary: Modern dating has become a costly, “date‑flation”‑driven activity that many people now have to budget for, according to a 2026 survey by JG Wentworth and a BMO Real Financial Progress Index report, which found the average all‑in date cost rose 12.5 % to $189—outpacing living expenses and pushing 86 % of US singles to delay or abandon dating. Low‑income earners are hit hardest, with one‑third of those making under $50,000 stopping entirely, while even high‑income individuals are taking breaks. This economic friction turns dating into a luxury, driving intentional but unequal participation, especially among Gen Z‑X men, who are increasingly opting out and sharing the strain on platforms like TikTok. The trend has fueled discussions around sugar babies and the broader financial realities of romance, suggesting that connection is no longer spontaneous but a costly, discretionary pursuit.
